text:
Maria G: Heads up — I merged the terraform module refactor PR that splits `infra/core` into `infra/providers` + `infra/k8s-modules`. After the merge, `terraform plan` in the staging workspace is failing with a provider lock mismatch and a bunch of moved resource addresses. Has anyone seen this pattern?

Kevin L: Yep, saw that in another repo. What error are you getting exactly? provider checksum mismatch or the usual "provider registry found but lockfile mismatch"?

Maria G: It's this: `Error: Incompatible lock file checksums` then `Run 'terraform providers lock' to update`. But running that in the repo root updates a lockfile that doesn't match some CI workspaces, and I don't want to blindly change the lockfile in master. Also many resources show up as needing to be recreated because the module path changed (module.infra -> module.k8s-modules).

Alex P: For the lockfile: we keep a single `terraform.lock.hcl` at repo root. You should regenerate it from the canonical workspace (staging-prod-ish). Command we usually use: `terraform init -upgrade && terraform providers lock -platform=linux_amd64`. Then commit the lockfile. But do not run `-upgrade` in workspaces with pinned provider versions unless you intend to.

Sophia R: Re: moved addresses — that's a state namespace change. You need `terraform state mv` to preserve resources when splitting modules. Example: `terraform state mv module.infra.aws_secret.example module.k8s-modules.aws_secret.example` run from the repo root workspace after fetching the new configuration. Do that in staging first.

Maria G: OK, I have a partial list of `state mv` commands. Two Qs: 1) should the lockfile be updated before doing the `state mv`? 2) CI runs `terraform plan` in parallel in multiple workspaces — will regenerating lockfile break CI until all workspaces are in sync?

Kevin L: 1) You can update the lockfile first in the staging workspace you plan to apply from — that ensures `init` picks the same provider binaries for plan/apply. 2) CI will fail in other workspaces that still have the old lockfile if they run `init` and detect a mismatch. Mitigation: push the lockfile update in the same PR as the state migration, then coordinate a short maintenance window or sequentially roll the workspaces.

Alex P: Another option is to vendor provider plugins in our internal mirror (we don't have that set up everywhere). Or pin exact provider versions in `required_providers` for the root module to avoid unexpected upgrades: `required_providers { aws = { source = "hashicorp/aws" version = "~> 4.65.0" } }`. That keeps `terraform providers lock` deterministic.

Maria G: Noted. I'll do: (a) regenerate lockfile locally in staging, (b) run `terraform state mv` for the moved secrets, (c) open a single PR with lockfile + state-move docs + plan output attached.

Kevin L: Sounds good. Small tip: run `terraform plan -out=tfplan` after `state mv` and attach the binary plan to the PR artifacts (or `terraform show -json tfplan > plan.json`) so reviewers can inspect.

Sophia R: Also check any modules that passed providers via `providers = {}` — moving modules may require updating provider aliases. If the k8s module used `kubernetes` provider from a module wrapper, validate `provider = kubernetes.svc` references.

Maria G: Will do. I'll also add a short notes section in the PR with the exact `state mv` commands I ran and why. Ping me @Maria G if you want to validate before I push.

infra-bot: CI: plan job for branch `maria/module-split` — queued. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

Kevin L: If anything goes sideways we can revert the module split commit and re-run plans. But moving state is safe if the `state mv` commands are correct. Happy to review the `state mv` list. :+1:

Maria G: Appreciate it — pushing the PR in ~30m.
